MD5 is not thread-safe, so each thread keeps its own instance: this avoids allocating/initializing a fresh crypto provider on every hash (the bulk-load hot path) while preserving the exact same digest produced by the former per-call MD5CryptoServiceProvider.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Model.RDFTermResolver
member.summary:
RDFTermResolver is the neutral abstraction that supplies, to the term-level parsers of RDFTurtle, the only two pieces of contextual information they actually need in order to materialize an RDF term: a base IRI (to resolve relative IRI references) and a prefix-to-namespace resolution function.
Decoupling these two responsibilities away from RDFGraph lets the very same term-level parsers (ParseURI, ParseQNameOrBoolean, ParseValue, ParseQuotedLiteral, ...) be reused verbatim by the SPARQL parser, which resolves base/prefixes from a query-local context instead of a graph.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Model.RDFTermResolver.BaseUri
member.summary: The base IRI used to resolve relative IRI references and bare-fragment IRIs (e.g. "#").

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Model.RDFTermResolver.ResolveNamespace(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a prefix label to its namespace IRI. An empty (or null) prefix label denotes the default namespace (the ":" prefix). Returns null when the prefix cannot be resolved.

summary.para: Pull-style reader with bounded LIFO pushback over a TextReader. Lets the Turtle/TriG parser peek and rewind a small number of UTF-16 chars without ever holding the full input in memory.

Capacity is sized for the worst-case parser pushback: ParseStatement reads up to 8 code points (16 UTF-16 chars if all supplementary) before deciding whether to rewind. 32 chars gives a 2x safety margin over that worst case.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver
member.summary: RDFGraphTermResolver is the graph-backed implementation of RDFTermResolver used while deserializing Turtle/TriG data into an RDFGraph. It reads from the wrapped graph LIVE (at call time): this is required because Turtle "@base"/"@prefix" directives mutate the graph context and the global namespace register WHILE the document is being parsed, and subsequent relative IRIs and prefixed names must resolve against the most recent state.

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.graph
member.summary: The graph being populated during deserialization, queried live for base/default-namespace.

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.declaredPrefixes
member.summary: Per-document prefix declarations (prefix label → namespace IRI), recorded as the document's @prefix/PREFIX directives are parsed and consulted BEFORE the global namespace register. This guarantees that a prefix declared in THIS document always resolves — even when it could not be added to the register (e.g. its IRI collides with an already-registered/reserved namespace), which would otherwise make a legitimately-declared prefix look undeclared and be wrongly rejected.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.#ctor(RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraph)
member.summary: Builds a graph-backed term resolver wrapping the given graph.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.BaseUri
member.summary: The base IRI is the graph's current context.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.RegisterDeclaredPrefix(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: Records a prefix declaration found in the document being deserialized, so it resolves regardless of whether it could also be added to the global namespace register.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Model.RDFGraphTermResolver.ResolveNamespace(System.String)
member.summary: Resolves a prefix label. An empty prefix maps to the graph's default context (base). A non-empty prefix is resolved first against THIS document's own declarations (so a declared prefix always wins), then against the global namespace register's well-known prefixes; it returns null when the label was neither declared in the document nor registered — the caller then raises an explicit parse error.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression
member.summary: RDFExistsExpression represents the SPARQL EXISTS built-in as a first-class value-expression: it tests whether a given group graph pattern produces at least one solution compatible with the current row, and yields the boolean typed literal true/false

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.GroupGraphPattern
member.summary: Group graph pattern to be evaluated on the RDF data source. As per SPARQL grammar (GroupGraphPattern ::= '{' ( SubSelect | GroupGraphPatternSub ) '}') it is either a (SubSelect) or a (GroupGraphPatternSub).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.PatternResults
member.summary: Results of the group graph pattern evaluation on the RDF data source. Being correlation-dependent it is not computed by the expression itself but PRE-EVALUATED once (per data source) by the query engine before the per-row expression evaluation starts (see RDFQueryEngine.PreEvaluateNestedExistsExpressions).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.IndexedTable
member.summary: The resultset for which was last built: lets the index be reused across all the rows of one expression application and rebuilt when a fresh evaluation assigns a new table.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.PatternResultsIndex
member.summary: Per variable column: maps each value's PatternMemberID to the set of PatternResults row indexes holding that value (columnName -> (valueMemberID -> resultRowIndexes)).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.#ctor(RDFSharp.Query.RDFSelectQuery)
member.summary: Builds an EXISTS expression on the given SubSelect group graph pattern

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.#ctor(RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternGroup)
member.summary: Builds an EXISTS expression on the given pattern group graph pattern

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.ToString
member.summary: Gives the string representation of the EXISTS expression

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.ApplyExpression(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Applies the EXISTS expression on the given datarow, returning the boolean typed literal true when the group graph pattern produced at least one result compatible with that row, false otherwise. "Compatible" means agreeing on every variable shared between the pattern results and the row. Instead of rescanning (and reparsing) the whole pattern resultset for each candidate row, we consult a hash index built once per resultset, turning each check into O(1) lookups.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.GetSharedVariables(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Returns the variable columns present both in the pattern results and in the given row: these are the columns on which EXISTS correlates the two sides (independent of the pattern's concrete shape).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.BuildPatternResultsIndex
member.summary: Lazily builds (once per pattern resultset) the hash index used by ApplyExpression. For every variable column of the pattern results, it maps each distinct value (by canonical member identity) to the set of pattern-result row indexes carrying that value. The index is keyed by the resultset's reference identity, so a fresh evaluation (which assigns a new PatternResults table) triggers a rebuild.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.FindNestedExistsExpressions(RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression)
member.summary: Walks the given expression tree and returns every nested anywhere within it (including the tree itself when it IS an EXISTS). This is the single point of knowledge about "how to locate EXISTS nodes inside an expression": the base stays clean (no virtuals), and the query engine relies on this to pre-evaluate every nested EXISTS before per-row evaluation.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression.CollectNestedExistsExpressions(RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression,System.Collections.Generic.List{RDFSharp.Query.RDFExistsExpression})
member.summary: Recursive accumulator backing : descends the structure exposed by the base class (LeftArgument/RightArgument, followed only when they are themselves expressions) plus the few side containers that hold expressions outside Left/Right (RDFInExpression.InTerms, RDFIfExpression's condition). When an EXISTS node is reached it is appended (and not descended into, being argument-less).

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFIriExpression
member.summary:
RDFIriExpression represents an IRI-building function to be applied on a query results table (it also backs the SPARQL URI alias).
MODEL LIMITATION. RDFSharp has no query-level BASE in its model, so relative IRIs cannot be resolved: this function returns a resource argument unchanged and turns a string literal into a resource only when the string is an ABSOLUTE IRI; any relative/invalid input yields an unbound result.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFNotExpression
member.summary: RDFNotExpression represents a logical negation (boolean "NOT") expression to be applied on a query results table. It lives inside the value-expression world, so it can be nested anywhere an expression is expected (e.g. to model "NOT IN" as "!( … IN … )", "NOT EXISTS" as "!EXISTS", or a negated FILTER as "FILTER(!( … ))").

RDFTimezoneExpression represents a datetime timezone function (returning an xsd:dayTimeDuration) to be applied on a query results table.

member.summary: RDFGroupByModifier represents an aggregator modifier to be applied on a query results table.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.PartitionConditions
member.summary: The GROUP BY conditions, in order: each is either a bare grouping variable ('GROUP BY ?v') or a grouping expression ('GROUP BY (expr AS ?v)' / anonymous '(expr)'). This is the SINGLE source of truth for grouping: the partition variables, the expressions to materialize and the synthetic (anonymous) columns are all read off these conditions (see ).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.Aggregators
member.summary: List of aggregators applied on the result groups. It also holds the automatic of each partition variable; use / to filter.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.EvaluableAggregators
member.summary: The aggregators that actually evaluate an aggregate function (COUNT/SUM/AVG/...): every aggregator except the automatic partition ones.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ProjectableAggregators
member.summary: The evaluable aggregators that ALSO surface as query result columns: the minus the hidden ones (which only feed a HAVING / projection expression).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.HavingExpression
member.summary: HAVING condition: a single, all-encompassing boolean expression evaluated on the RESULT table (after projection), keeping a grouped row only when it evaluates to true. It expresses the full SPARQL HAVING power (disjunctions, aggregate on the right-hand side, non-comparison constraints, an aggregate not present in the SELECT projection). Aggregates referenced here read their already-materialized columns through a plain .

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.#ctor
member.summary: Builds an implicit-grouping modifier (no partition conditions): every solution falls into a single group, so the aggregates added to it are computed over the WHOLE result set (SPARQL implicit grouping, i.e. an aggregate projection without a GROUP BY clause).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.#ctor(System.Collections.Generic.List{RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable})
member.summary: Builds a GroupBy modifier on the given variables

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ToString
member.summary: Gives the string representation of the modifier. A bare partition variable prints as '?v'; a GROUP BY expression prints as '(expr AS ?v)' when named or '(expr)' when anonymous.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.PrintPartitionCondition(RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByCondition)
member.summary: Prints a single GROUP BY condition (bare variable, named expression or anonymous expression).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.AddAggregator(RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator)
member.summary: Adds the given aggregator to the modifier

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.SetHavingExpression(RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression)
member.summary:
Sets the HAVING condition: a single boolean expression evaluated on the result table, keeping only the grouped rows for which it holds. This is the fluent-API counterpart of the SPARQL HAVING clause, with the full expressive power (disjunctions, reversed comparisons, non-comparison constraints).
To reference an aggregate inside the expression, point at the aggregator's projection variable with a plain (e.g. for '(COUNT(?e) AS ?cnt)', reference '?cnt'): the value is read from that already-computed column. There is no need to restate the aggregate function call.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ReprintHiddenAggregateCalls(System.String)
member.summary:
Re-prints, inside an already-rendered expression (a HAVING condition or a projection expression), any aggregate the parser had to materialize behind the scenes — a HIDDEN aggregator, used for an aggregate referenced in HAVING but not projected, or one nested in a projection expression — as its ORIGINAL call (e.g. "AVG(?g)") instead of the synthetic column name it is evaluated through.
This mirrors how the printer already renders other synthetic columns by their definition rather than their internal name (GROUP BY '(expr)', SUM(?x + ?y)). Only the reserved hidden-aggregator column names are substituted, longest first (so '?__HAVINGAGG_10' is not corrupted by '?__HAVINGAGG_1'), so it can never touch a user variable or alias.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.AddPartitionVariable(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable)
member.summary: Adds a bare GROUP BY variable condition ('GROUP BY ?v').

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.AddPartitionExpression(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable,RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Adds a GROUP BY condition over an expression: a fresh partition variable (named '(expr AS ?v)' or anonymous '(expr)') whose values are materialized from the expression before partitioning.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.AddPartitionConditionInternal(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable,RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Shared GROUP BY condition registration: adds the condition (once per variable) and its mandatory partition aggregator. Everything else about the condition — the expression to materialize, whether it is named, and whether it is an anonymous synthetic column — lives on the itself.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.CollectComputedColumns
member.summary: The (synthetic) columns to materialize into the working table BEFORE partitioning, so that grouping and aggregation keep operating over single columns: every GROUP BY expression condition (e.g. GROUP BY (?x+?y)) plus every aggregate-over-expression (e.g. SUM(?x+?y)). Each entry pairs the target column with the expression producing its values, and flags whether the column is anonymous grouping scratch to be dropped.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ApplyModifier(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Applies the modifier on the given table

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.MaterializeComputedColumns(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Builds a working table augmented with the computed columns: each declared expression is evaluated per-row and stored in a (synthetic) column, so partitioning/aggregation can keep operating over single columns. Returns the original table unchanged when there is nothing to materialize.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.DropSyntheticColumns(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Removes the anonymous GROUP BY expression columns from the result table (they are an internal scratch).

member.summary: Performs consistency checks

member.summary: Executes partition algorithm

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ExecuteProjectionAlgorythm
member.summary: Executes projection algorythm

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.ExecuteFilterAlgorythm(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFGroupByModifier.GetPartitionKey(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Calculates the partition key on the given table row. The key is built by appending, for every partition variable, "name§PV§value" (an UNBOUND value contributes an empty string) and joining the pieces with "§PK§". The exact layout MUST be preserved: the projection step splits the key back on these very placeholders to recover the bindings (see RDFAggregator.UpdateProjectionTable).

member.summary: RDFOrderByModifier is a modifier which applies a sort on the results of a SELECT query for the given ordering key.

member.summary: Expression to be ordered (the ordering key). A bare-variable ORDER BY is represented as an over that variable.

member.summary: Flavor of ordering (ASC/DESC)

member.summary: Builds an OrderBy modifier of the given flavor on the given variable (ergonomic ctor: the variable is wrapped into an , which becomes the single stored ordering key).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOrderByModifier.#ctor(RDFSharp.Query.RDFExpression,RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryEnums.RDFOrderByFlavors)

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOrderByModifier.ToString
member.summary: Gives the string representation of the modifier (e.g. "ASC(?x)", "DESC(STRLEN(?x))"). For the bare-variable case the variable expression renders as "?x", so the output stays identical to the historical form.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOrderByModifier.ApplyModifier(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Applies the modifier on the given table (stable Ordinal sort on the ordering key's column, UNBOUND sorts smallest; keys whose column is absent are ignored). In the live pipeline the ORDER BY sort is applied by the projection step, so this is exercised mainly by direct callers and tests. The ordering key column is resolved the same way as the live pipeline: a bare variable sorts on its existing column, any other expression is materialized into a (synthetic) column, sorted, then dropped.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOrderByModifier.EnsureSortColumn(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Ensures the ordering key is available as a single column of the given table and returns its name. A bare variable reuses its existing column; any other expression is evaluated into a fresh (synthetic) column (same primitives the GROUP BY path uses to materialize computed columns). This is the single locus where the variable-vs-expression discrimination lives.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAddOperation
member.summary: RDFAddOperation is the SPARQL "ADD" graph-management operation implementation (ADD 'SILENT'? GraphOrDefault TO GraphOrDefault): it inserts all the triples of the source graph into the destination graph, leaving both the source and the pre-existing destination data in place. A null context (on either side) denotes the DEFAULT graph; a non-null context denotes a named graph. Being a two-graph operation, it is meaningful only on a context-aware store.

summary.para: RDFOperationSet models a SPARQL 1.1 UPDATE request made of MORE than one operation, i.e. the chain of ';'-separated operations of the grammar Update ::= Prologue ( Update1 ( ';' Update )? )?. It is a thin, composition-based wrapper over an ORDERED list of instances.

Applying a set to a graph/store runs its operations IN ORDER against the SAME mutable data source, so the effects of an earlier operation are visible to the later ones (e.g. an INSERT DATA followed by a DELETE WHERE that matches the freshly inserted triples). The returned per-operation results mirror positionally (ordinal semantics: the i-th result is the outcome of the i-th operation).

Atomicity is BEST-EFFORT and explicitly NOT transactional: there is no rollback. If an operation in the middle of the chain throws, the mutations already applied by the operations preceding it remain in the data source. Callers that need all-or-nothing semantics must snapshot/restore the data source themselves.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator
member.summary: RDFAggregator represents an aggregation function applied by a GroupBy modifier

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.Metadata
member.summary: The aggregator's metadata: the aggregated argument (variable or expression), the projection target, and the distinct/hidden flags. Grouped into one descriptor so the aggregator class itself stays focused on behavior (partition/projection execution) rather than carrying a flat bag of definition fields. See .

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.Context
member.summary: The context for keeping track of aggregator's evaluation

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ProjectionKeyPlaceholder
member.summary: Delimiter separating a partition-variable chunk from the next inside a partition key

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ProjectionValuePlaceholder
member.summary: Delimiter separating a partition variable's name from its value inside a partition key

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.#ctor(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable,RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable)
member.summary: Builds an aggregator on the given variable and with the given projection name

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.AggregatorFunction
member.summary: The aggregate function as it appears in SPARQL — e.g. "COUNT(?e)", "AVG(DISTINCT ?g)", "GROUP_CONCAT(?x; SEPARATOR=\",\")", "COUNT(*)" — WITHOUT the surrounding "(... AS ?proj)". Each concrete value-aggregator provides its own; the base (and the partition aggregator) has none.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ToString
member.summary: Gives the string representation of the aggregator function: "(call AS ?proj)", or the empty string when the aggregator has no call form (the partition aggregator).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.AggregatorArgument
member.summary: The printed form of the aggregated argument: the original expression when the aggregator was built over an expression (SUM(?x + ?y)), otherwise the bare aggregated variable. Used by every aggregator's ToString.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.MakeExpressionVariable(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable)
member.summary: Builds the (synthetic) aggregator variable backing an aggregate-over-expression (e.g. SUM(?x + ?y)): a reserved name derived from the projection variable, into which the GroupBy modifier materializes the expression's per-row values so the aggregation machinery keeps operating over a single column.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.GetAggregateCallString
member.summary: The aggregate function call (e.g. "COUNT(?e)") used to re-print an aggregate referenced inside a composite expression (HAVING / projection) without leaking the synthetic projection-column name.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ResetContext
member.summary: Resets the aggregator's execution context, so that the same aggregator (and the query owning it) can be safely re-executed without carrying over state from a previous run (which would otherwise corrupt sums, counters and caches)

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ExecutePartition(System.String,RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Executes the partition on the given table row

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ExecuteProjectionTable(System.Collections.Generic.List{RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable})
member.summary: Executes the projection producing result's table

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.UpdateProjectionTable(System.String,RDFSharp.Query.RDFTable)
member.summary: Helps in finalization step by updating the projection's result table

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.GetRowValueAsNumber(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Gets the row value for the aggregator as number

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.GetRowValueAsTypedLiteral(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)
member.summary: Gets the aggregated variable's value on the given row as a NUMERIC typed literal, preserving its original datatype (so MIN/MAX/SUM can keep/promote the genuine type). Returns null when the cell is unbound or its value is not a numeric typed literal.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.ParseTypedLiteralAsDouble(RDFSharp.Model.RDFTypedLiteral)
member.summary: Parses a numeric typed literal to double for ordering comparisons (owl:rational is evaluated first)

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.GetRowValueAsString(RDFSharp.Query.RDFTableRow)

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator.Distinct
member.summary: Sets the aggregator to discard duplicates

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata
member.summary: RDFAggregatorMetadata bundles the DEFINITION of an aggregator (what it aggregates, where it projects, and its distinct/hidden flags), keeping it together as one descriptor instead of a flat bag of fields scattered on . It carries data only — polymorphic behavior (e.g. the aggregate function) and execution state (the Context) stay on the aggregator.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.AggregatorVariable
member.summary: Variable aggregated by the aggregator, when the argument is a bare variable (e.g. SUM(?x)). For an expression argument it is the (synthetic) column the expression is materialized into.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.AggregatorExpression
member.summary: Expression aggregated by the aggregator, when the argument is not a bare variable (e.g. SUM(?x + ?y)). When set, the GroupBy modifier materializes it into the (synthetic) column before partitioning, and the printer re-emits the original expression instead of the synthetic variable.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.ProjectionVariable
member.summary: Variable used for projection of the aggregator's results.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.IsDistinct
member.summary: Whether the aggregator discards duplicates (DISTINCT).

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.IsHidden
member.summary: Whether the aggregator exists ONLY to feed a composite expression (a free HAVING condition, or a projection like '?x + COUNT(?y)') rather than to be projected as a query result column. The GroupBy modifier still computes its value into a (synthetic) column, but the engine keeps it out of the output projection.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorMetadata.#ctor(RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable,RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable)
member.summary: Builds the metadata for an aggregator on the given aggregated variable and projection name.
member.exception: When either variable is null.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorPartitionState
member.summary: RDFAggregatorPartitionState holds the running aggregation state of a single partition: the current result and how many rows have been folded into it so far. It replaces the former Dictionary<string,object> keyed by the literal strings "ExecutionResult"/"ExecutionCounter", removing - on every aggregated row - two string-keyed dictionary lookups and the boxing of the counter.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorPartitionState.ExecutionResult
member.summary: Running result of the aggregation for this partition. It stays an object because its concrete type is aggregator-dependent: a double for COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX over numbers, a string for GROUP_CONCAT/ SAMPLE/PARTITION and for MIN/MAX over strings.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorPartitionState.ExecutionCounter
member.summary: Number of rows folded into this partition so far (used e.g. by AVG). A plain double, never boxed.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorPartitionState.IsArithmeticallyPoisoned
member.summary: Whether this partition is arithmetically POISONED: a non-numeric row (or a numeric overflow) was encountered while aggregating numbers, so the result is undefined and the partition projects an unbound value.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregatorPartitionState.#ctor(System.Object)
member.summary: Builds the partition state seeded with the given initial result (counter starts at zero)

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService
member.summary:
RDFService is a first-class algebra node modeling a SPARQL SERVICE graph pattern: it delegates the evaluation of an inner group graph pattern to a remote SPARQL endpoint (federated query).
SPARQL grammar:
[59] ServiceGraphPattern ::= 'SERVICE' 'SILENT'? VarOrIri GroupGraphPattern [107] VarOrIri ::= Var | iri

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.Endpoint
member.summary: The single, reusable remote endpoint queried by this SERVICE. For a concrete (IRI) endpoint its is fixed; for a variable endpoint it is a reusable carrier whose the engine overwrites for every bound IRI (so the runtime never instantiates a fresh endpoint per binding). It also carries any authorization headers and query parameters set on it.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.EndpointVariable
P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.InnerPattern
member.summary: The inner group graph pattern delegated to the remote endpoint. As per SPARQL grammar (GroupGraphPattern ::= '{' ( SubSelect | GroupGraphPatternSub ) '}') it is any : a , an (SubSelect), a binary algebra tree (), or a nested .

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.QueryOptions
member.summary: Options driving the remote query. SERVICE SILENT maps to (errors yield an empty result instead of throwing); the default behavior throws on remote errors.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.IsOptional
member.summary: Flag indicating that this SERVICE participates in the surrounding join as an OPTIONAL branch (OPTIONAL { SERVICE … }): the engine left-joins its result table instead of inner-joining it.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.IsSilent
member.summary: Tells whether the SERVICE was declared SILENT (errors yield an empty result instead of throwing).

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Query.RDFService.VariableEndpointPlaceholder
member.summary: Placeholder address assigned to the reusable endpoint of a variable SERVICE: it is never queried as-is, because the engine overwrites it with each concrete IRI bound to .

member.exception: When the endpoint or the inner pattern is null.

member.summary: Builds a SERVICE delegating the given inner pattern to the endpoint bound, at runtime, to the given variable (SERVICE ?ep {…}). The engine resolves the variable against the surrounding solution bindings and queries each distinct IRI reusing a single endpoint instance.
member.exception: When the variable or the inner pattern is null.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFValues.Bindings
member.summary: Dictionary of bindings representing the SPARQL values (one entry per declared variable, mapping it to its column of values; a null entry in a column is the special UNDEF binding). It is EMPTY for the degenerate NIL data block (VALUES () { ... }), which declares no variable at all.

member.name: P:RDFSharp.Query.RDFValues.NilRowsCount
member.summary: Number of empty-domain rows of a NIL data block (VALUES () { () () }): with zero declared variables the row cardinality cannot be derived from any column, so it is carried explicitly here. It is meaningful ONLY when is empty (otherwise the row count is the column length). Each such row is an identity solution mapping: 0 rows annihilate the join (zero solutions), 1 row is the identity (no-op), N rows duplicate every solution N-fold (multiset semantics).

member.summary: Tells (conservatively) whether EVERY cell of the table is bound, i.e. the table carries NO UNBOUND cell anywhere. It is a SAFE-polarity hint: the default is false ("not known to be fully bound"), and it is raised to true ONLY by producers that provably emit no nulls (a triple/quad pattern population, and the inner-join of two fully-bound tables). Any lowers it back to false, because widening introduces an UNBOUND cell on existing rows (and a freshly projected column may stay unbound). It lets pick the cheaper strict inner-join when a join is provably pure-inner (no UNBOUND in the common columns, non-optional right); when in doubt it stays false and the safe outer-join is used.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationEngine.EvaluateCopyMoveAddOperation(System.String,System.Boolean,System.Uri,System.Uri,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,RDFSharp.Model.RDFDataSource)
member.summary:
Evaluates a source→destination graph-management operation (ADD/COPY/MOVE) on the given RDF datasource. These are two-graph operations: they are expressed as a SEQUENCE of existing UPDATE steps and run, in order, against the same store via — no bespoke mutation logic.
ADD (clearDestination=false, dropSource=false): INSERT the source triples into the destination.
COPY (clearDestination=true, dropSource=false): clear the destination, then INSERT the source triples.
MOVE (clearDestination=true, dropSource=true): clear the destination, INSERT the source triples, then clear the source.
A null context denotes the DEFAULT graph. Source equal to destination is a no-op. A contextless graph datasource cannot represent these two-graph operations, so it raises an error (suppressed when SILENT).
member.exception: When applied to a graph (non-SILENT): these operations require a context-aware store.

summary.para: LOOP SAFETY (the chief hazard of recursive path evaluation): the recursion is on the FINITE, ACYCLIC step tree, so it always terminates regardless of the data. The only cycles are in the DATA, under +/*: there the sub-relation is first materialized into an EXPLICIT, FINITE adjacency map and the closure is always delegated to (Tarjan SCC → acyclic condensation), which is provably cycle-proof. The engine NEVER walks the data graph recursively for a closure.

Federation members that are SPARQL endpoints are delegated to their own remote SPARQL engine.

A variable start over a single Link that requires at least one hop (no zero-length match) is pruned to the nodes actually having an outgoing edge on the step property (its domain). In every other case a zero-length match may be possible, so all nodes in the datasource remain candidate seeds.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFPathEngine.RDFTransitiveClosureIndex
member.summary:
Precomputed all-pairs transitive reachability over a single binary relation, used to answer "+" (and, with the start node added by the caller, "*") in amortized output time.
THE PROBLEM. A property path such as "?x knows+ ?y" asks, for every node x, the set of nodes reachable from x by following one or more "knows" edges — i.e. the transitive closure of the relation. Computing this with an independent breadth-first search per node costs O(V·(V+E)) and recomputes the same sub-closures over and over; on cyclic data it also has to carefully avoid looping forever.
THE IDEA. Two nodes that sit on a common cycle reach exactly the same set of nodes (each can reach the other and therefore everything the other reaches). Such mutually-reachable groups are the graph's STRONGLY-CONNECTED COMPONENTS (SCCs): maximal sets where every node reaches every other node. If we collapse each SCC to a single super-node we obtain the CONDENSATION graph, which is always acyclic (a DAG) — any cycle would, by definition, have been swallowed into one SCC. On a DAG reachability is trivial to accumulate with one pass in topological order, and every node of an SCC inherits the very same reachable set, so the closure is computed once per component instead of once per node.
THE ALGORITHM. runs Tarjan's SCC algorithm (a single DFS, here made iterative to survive very deep chains without blowing the call stack) to label every node with its component, then builds the condensation edges and propagates reachability across them. Querying a node () is then just "emit my own component's members if it is cyclic, plus the members of every downstream component".
THE "+" SEMANTICS. "+" requires at least one hop, so a node reaches ITSELF only if a non-trivial cycle brings it back: that happens exactly when its component is cyclic — either it has more than one member, or it is a single node carrying a self-loop edge (x knows x). A singleton component without a self-loop never reaches itself. The caller turns "+" into "*" simply by adding the start node itself (the zero-hop reflexive match).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFPathEngine.RDFTransitiveClosureIndex.EnumerateReachableNodes(RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternMember)
member.summary: Enumerates every term reachable from the given node in one or more hops, without duplicates.
member.remarks: The result is the union of two disjoint families of nodes, so no de-duplication is needed: (1) the node's own component, emitted only when that component is cyclic (the "reaches itself" case of "+"); and (2) the members of every component reachable downstream in the condensation. These are disjoint because a node belongs to exactly one component, and a component never appears among its own downstream reachable components (the condensation is acyclic).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryOptimizer.ReorderPatternGroupByJoinGraph(System.Collections.Generic.List{RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternGroupMember},System.Int32,System.Int32,RDFSharp.Model.RDFDataSource)
member.summary: Reorders, in place, a block of inner-join patterns using a greedy join-graph heuristic that keeps the intermediate results small. It grows a "join frontier": it starts from the most selective pattern, then repeatedly appends the pattern that is CONNECTED to the variables bound so far (to avoid cartesian products) and that should grow the intermediate the least - preferring patterns that introduce fewer NEW variables (they behave as filters) and, on a tie, the more selective one. Disconnected patterns are deferred; when one is unavoidable, the most selective starts a new branch.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryOptimizer.SelectNextPattern(System.Collections.Generic.List{RDFSharp.Query.RDFPattern},System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary{RDFSharp.Query.RDFPattern,System.Int64},System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.String})
member.summary: Selects, among the still-unplaced patterns, the index of the next pattern to execute. A pattern is "connected" when it shares at least one variable with the already-bound frontier; connected patterns are always preferred over disconnected ones (which would force a cartesian product). Within the same connectivity, the ranking is: fewer NEW variables first (a pattern that binds nothing new is a pure filter that shrinks the intermediate), then lower static cardinality, then earliest declared position (so the result is deterministic and stable). The very first pick (empty frontier) has no connectivity to exploit yet, so it is ranked purely by cardinality (most selective seed).

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser
member.summary:
CLEAR/LOAD half of the SPARQL UPDATE parser: the CLEAR and LOAD operations — the two UPDATE forms that carry no triple template and no WHERE clause, only graph references and the optional SILENT flag.
SPARQL grammar:
Load ::= 'LOAD' 'SILENT'? iri ( 'INTO' GraphRef )? Clear ::= 'CLEAR' 'SILENT'? GraphRefAll GraphRef ::= 'GRAPH' iri GraphRefAll ::= GraphRef | 'DEFAULT' | 'NAMED' | 'ALL'

COPY/MOVE/ADD third of the SPARQL UPDATE graph-management parser: the source→destination operations, sharing one body grammar (a GraphOrDefault pair separated by 'TO', plus the optional SILENT flag) and differing only in the concrete operation they build.
SPARQL grammar:
Copy ::= 'COPY' 'SILENT'? GraphOrDefault 'TO' GraphOrDefault Move ::= 'MOVE' 'SILENT'? GraphOrDefault 'TO' GraphOrDefault Add ::= 'ADD' 'SILENT'? GraphOrDefault 'TO' GraphOrDefault GraphOrDefault ::= 'DEFAULT' | 'GRAPH'? iri

CREATE/DROP half of the SPARQL UPDATE graph-management parser: the two operations whose body is a single graph reference (plus the optional SILENT flag), with no triple template and no source→destination pair.
SPARQL grammar:
Create ::= 'CREATE' 'SILENT'? GraphRef Drop ::= 'DROP' 'SILENT'? GraphRefAll GraphRef ::= 'GRAPH' iri GraphRefAll ::= GraphRef | 'DEFAULT' | 'NAMED' | 'ALL'

DATA half of the SPARQL UPDATE parser: the INSERT DATA and DELETE DATA operations — the two forms whose body is a QuadData (a set of GROUND triples and/or GRAPH iri { … } quad blocks) with no WHERE clause and no variables.
SPARQL grammar:
InsertData ::= 'INSERT DATA' QuadData DeleteData ::= 'DELETE DATA' QuadData QuadData ::= '{' Quads '}' Quads ::= TriplesTemplate? ( ('GRAPH' VarOrIri '{' TriplesTemplate? '}') '.'? TriplesTemplate? )*
The QuadData is collected through the context's template sink (), reusing the whole triple machine while preserving ground triples; a GRAPH iri { … } block sets the active context so its triples are emitted as four-argument quads. The "DATA" forms forbid variables: each collected pattern is added through the model's ground-only AddInsert/DeleteTemplate, which rejects any pattern carrying a variable (including a variable graph context). Property paths are likewise rejected (QuadData has no path production).

Modify/WHERE half of the SPARQL UPDATE parser: the template-plus-WHERE operations that delete and/or insert the bindings produced by a WHERE clause. Three model classes are produced: (DELETE-only), (INSERT-only), and (both).
SPARQL grammar:
DeleteWhere ::= 'DELETE WHERE' QuadPattern Modify ::= ('WITH' iri)? ( DeleteClause InsertClause? | InsertClause ) UsingClause* 'WHERE' GroupGraphPattern DeleteClause ::= 'DELETE' QuadPattern InsertClause ::= 'INSERT' QuadPattern UsingClause ::= 'USING' ( 'NAMED'? iri )
The QuadPattern templates (which, unlike QuadData, may carry variables) are read with the shared and attached through the model's NON-ground AddDelete/InsertTemplate; the WHERE clause reuses the full query . Model-imposed limit: WITH and USING [NAMED] address a dataset the flat operation model has no slot for, so both are rejected as non-representable.

summary.para: RDFOperationParser turns a SPARQL 1.1 UPDATE command string into the corresponding object-model instance. It is the UPDATE-side counterpart of : it owns the operation grammar (LOAD / CLEAR / INSERT … / DELETE …) and its dispatcher, while REUSING the query parser's shared infrastructure — the lexer (, via using static), the parsing context (), the prologue parser () and the term-reader — so that nothing is duplicated.

SPARQL grammar (the UPDATE side): Update ::= Prologue ( Update1 ( ';' Update )? )?. The flat model represents ONE operation per object, so a chain of ';'-separated operations is not representable: a single operation is parsed and any following one is rejected (see ).

member.summary: Parses the body of a DELETE DATA operation (the 'DELETE' 'DATA' keywords have already been consumed by the dispatcher): the prologue prefixes plus the QuadData ground templates.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseQuadsTemplate(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,System.String)
member.summary:
Parses a QuadData block — '{' Quads '}' — into a flat list of template instances (three-argument triples in the default graph, four-argument quads inside a GRAPH iri { … } block). The template sink is installed for the duration of the block and removed afterwards, regardless of outcome.
Property paths are not allowed (QuadData has no path production): they are caught as members of the scratch group they would have populated. The "DATA" groundness restriction is NOT enforced here — it is applied by the caller's ground-only AddInsert/DeleteTemplate, which gives a precise error.
member.returns: The template patterns read from the block, in document order.
member.exception: When the block is malformed or contains a property path.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseQuadsGraphBlock(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternGroup,System.String)
member.summary: Parses a GRAPH iri { TriplesTemplate? } quad block (the 'GRAPH' keyword has already been consumed): the graph context is fixed for the duration of the inner triples so they are emitted as four-argument quads, then the enclosing context is restored. An empty block is legal (it simply yields no quads, unlike a query GRAPH whose empty group is rejected).
member.exception: When the graph specifier or the braces are malformed.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseInsertWhereOperation(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses an INSERT-only Modify operation (the 'INSERT' keyword has already been consumed and is known NOT to be 'INSERT DATA'): INSERT QuadPattern UsingClause* 'WHERE' GroupGraphPattern.
member.exception: When the template/WHERE is malformed, or a USING clause is present.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseDeleteWhereOperation(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary:
Parses a DELETE-led Modify operation (the 'DELETE' keyword has already been consumed and is known NOT to be 'DELETE DATA'). Handles all three shapes:
DELETE WHERE QuadPattern — the short form: the template IS the WHERE pattern.
DELETE QuadPattern UsingClause* 'WHERE' GroupGraphPattern — delete-only Modify.
DELETE QuadPattern INSERT QuadPattern UsingClause* 'WHERE' GroupGraphPattern — delete+insert.
member.exception: When the template/WHERE is malformed, or a USING clause is present.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseDeleteWhereShortForm(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the short form DELETE WHERE QuadPattern (the 'DELETE' 'WHERE' keywords have already been consumed): the QuadPattern triples serve BOTH as the delete templates and as the WHERE pattern. Ground triples are naturally dropped from the WHERE group by (which keeps only variable-bearing patterns), the correct behaviour for a graph pattern.
member.exception: When the QuadPattern is malformed or contains a property path.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.RejectUsingClause(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Rejects a UsingClause (USING [NAMED] iri): deliberately NOT supported, because USING (like FROM/WITH) tells a SPARQL endpoint which dataset the operation's WHERE should match, whereas RDFSharp evaluates over the source you provide; the same scoping is expressed with GRAPH patterns. The keyword is peeked and pushed back before throwing.
member.exception: When the next token is the USING keyword.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseOperation(System.String,RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryOptions)

summary.para: Parses a complete SPARQL 1.1 UPDATE command string into the corresponding object-model instance. Like it builds a fresh parsing context, consumes the (possibly empty) BASE/PREFIX prologue, then dispatches on the operation keyword.

member.exception: When the text is empty, the operation keyword is missing/unknown/non-representable, or the body is malformed.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseOperationSet(System.String,RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryOptions)

summary.para: Parses a complete chain of ;-separated SPARQL 1.1 UPDATE operations into an , the only model able to represent more than one operation. This is the multi-operation counterpart of : it shares the very same per-operation dispatcher (), looping over the ; separators of the grammar Update ::= Prologue ( Update1 ( ';' Update )? )? until end-of-input.

The prologue is (re)parsed before each operation onto the SAME parsing context, so PREFIX/BASE declarations accumulate and stay in scope for the operations that follow them, exactly as the SPARQL specification mandates for an operation chain. A single trailing ; is tolerated.

member.exception: When the text is empty, an operation keyword is missing/unknown/non-representable, a body is malformed, or two operations are not separated by ';'.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseSingleOperation(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Reads the keyword run that names ONE SPARQL UPDATE operation (the prologue must already have been consumed) and dispatches on it, returning the parsed . This is the shared per-operation core used both by the single-operation and by the chain-aware ; it does NOT enforce what (if anything) follows the operation, leaving that policy to the caller.
member.exception: When the operation keyword is missing/unknown/non-representable, or the body is malformed.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.RejectTrailingOperationContent(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Requires that nothing significant follows the parsed operation, beyond an optional single trailing ;. The SPARQL grammar allows a chain of ;-separated operations, but the flat model holds exactly one operation per object, so a second operation is rejected as non-representable rather than silently dropped ( does not enforce end-of-input itself).
member.exception: When a second operation, or any other content, follows.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFOperationParser.ParseOperationIri(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,System.String)
member.summary: Parses a single iri in operation position (a LOAD/CLEAR graph reference) and returns it as an absolute . The IRI is read through the shared term-reader (so prologue BASE/PREFIX resolution applies). A variable, a literal or a blank node in this position is invalid.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser
member.summary:
Aggregate-function half of the SPARQL parser: reads a single SPARQL aggregate (COUNT/SUM/MIN/MAX/AVG/SAMPLE/GROUP_CONCAT) into a function-agnostic descriptor, then materializes it into a concrete once the projection variable is known. Shared by the SELECT-projection path ((AGG(?v) AS ?p)) and by the HAVING path (which only needs to MATCH an aggregate, not project it).
SPARQL grammar:
[127] Aggregate ::= 'COUNT' '(' 'DISTINCT'? ( '*' | Expression ) ')' | ('SUM'|'MIN'|'MAX'|'AVG'|'SAMPLE') '(' 'DISTINCT'? Expression ')' | 'GROUP_CONCAT' '(' 'DISTINCT'? Expression ( ';' 'SEPARATOR' '=' String )? ')'
Model-imposed limits (the flat can only aggregate over a SINGLE variable): COUNT(*) and any aggregate whose argument is an expression (e.g. SUM(?x + ?y)) are NOT representable and raise an explicit . MIN/MAX are mapped to the flavor: SPARQL has no syntax to choose between numeric and string ordering, so the common numeric case is the default.

ASK-form half of the SPARQL parser: the body of an ASK query — its WHERE clause plus any trailing solution modifiers and inline data — assembled into an once the 'ASK' keyword has been dispatched. ASK asks whether the (modified) solution sequence has at least one solution.
SPARQL grammar: AskQuery ::= 'ASK' DatasetClause* WhereClause SolutionModifier, followed by the query-level ValuesClause ([4] Query). The solution modifiers do affect the boolean answer (e.g. LIMIT 0, an OFFSET past the last row, or a HAVING that drops every group all make ASK false), so they are parsed and applied rather than rejected.
Model-imposed limit: a DatasetClause (FROM / FROM NAMED) is spec-legal but NOT representable (RDFSharp is an evaluation engine over a given data source, not an endpoint), so it raises an explicit rather than being silently dropped.

BIND / inline-data (VALUES) half of the SPARQL parser. Both are s: they do not produce a sibling algebra member but are absorbed into the surrounding pattern group, exactly like FILTER. BIND(expr AS ?v) attaches a computed binding; VALUES attaches an inline data table (single-variable compact form, or multi-variable extended form, with the UNDEF placeholder).

CONSTRUCT-form half of the SPARQL parser: the body of a CONSTRUCT query — its graph TEMPLATE plus the WHERE clause — assembled into an once the 'CONSTRUCT' keyword has been dispatched. CONSTRUCT builds an RDF graph by instantiating the template once per WHERE solution.
SPARQL grammar:
ConstructQuery ::= 'CONSTRUCT' ( ConstructTemplate DatasetClause* WhereClause SolutionModifier | DatasetClause* 'WHERE' '{' TriplesTemplate? '}' SolutionModifier ) ConstructTemplate ::= '{' ConstructTriples? '}' ConstructTriples ::= TriplesSameSubject ( '.' ConstructTriples? )?
Both forms are handled: the LONG form CONSTRUCT { template } WHERE { … } and the SHORT form CONSTRUCT WHERE { triples }, where the template coincides with the WHERE triples.
Model-imposed limits (the flat has no dataset and only LIMIT/OFFSET modifier slots): a DatasetClause (FROM / FROM NAMED) and the ORDER BY / GROUP BY / HAVING solution modifiers are spec-legal but NOT representable, so each raises an explicit rather than being silently dropped. Property paths and non-triple elements (FILTER/OPTIONAL/…) are not allowed inside a template by the grammar and are likewise rejected.

DESCRIBE-form half of the SPARQL parser: the body of a DESCRIBE query — its describe-terms (variables/IRIs or the * wildcard), an OPTIONAL WHERE clause, and the trailing solution modifiers — assembled into an once the 'DESCRIBE' keyword has been dispatched.
SPARQL grammar:
DescribeQuery ::= 'DESCRIBE' ( VarOrIri+ | '*' ) DatasetClause* WhereClause? SolutionModifier VarOrIri ::= Var | iri
Model-imposed limits (the flat has no dataset and only LIMIT/OFFSET modifier slots): a DatasetClause (FROM / FROM NAMED) and the ORDER BY / GROUP BY / HAVING solution modifiers are spec-legal but NOT representable, so each raises an explicit rather than being silently dropped.

Built-in-call dispatch and lexer helpers for the FILTER/expression half of the SPARQL parser (phase F6). maps each SPARQL 1.1 built-in keyword onto its RDFSharp expression class; the helpers below add the multi-character operator and keyword lexing the expression grammar needs on top of the single-character primitives already defined in the core parser.

summary.para: FILTER + expression half of the SPARQL parser (phase F6). This partial holds everything needed to turn a SPARQL Constraint (the body of a FILTER) into the engine's filter/expression object model.

ONE EXPRESSION GRAMMAR. FILTER logic is modelled with a SINGLE representation: a boolean wrapped once in an (the only bridge from the value-expression world to the FILTER pattern-group-member world). The boolean connectives live entirely inside the expression world: || → , && → , ! → . The parser is the SPARQL operator-precedence ladder || > && > relational > additive > multiplicative > unary > primary: comparisons become , arithmetic becomes the math expressions, and the leaves dispatch onto the ~50 SPARQL 1.1 built-in expression classes.

THE BRACKET. A bare Constraint is a single BuiltInCall/FunctionCall parsed at the relational (ValueLogical) level, so top-level ||/&& are NOT accepted without parentheses (as the SPARQL grammar requires). A ( opens a BrackettedExpression parsed by the full expression ladder, so (?a && ?b) is a boolean expression and (?x+1) > 2 is a comparison over a bracketed arithmetic expression — both wrapped once into a single .

EXISTS COMPOSABILITY. EXISTS / NOT EXISTS are first-class value-expressions (, with NOT EXISTS = !EXISTS via ), so they compose with &&/||/! and appear anywhere an expression is expected (FILTER, BIND, projection, ORDER BY, GROUP BY/HAVING). Each carries a full group graph pattern (a or a SubSelect), so EXISTS over multi-triple / UNION / OPTIONAL groups is supported.

member.summary:
GeoSPARQL function-call dispatch for the SPARQL parser (phase F6b). SPARQL has no keyword for the GeoSPARQL functions: they are invoked through their IRI (e.g. geof:sfWithin(?a, ?b)), so they reach the parser as an iriOrFunction primary rather than as a BuiltInCall. This partial maps each recognised geof: / geosparql: function IRI onto its RDFSharp geo-expression class; any other function IRI is rejected with a precise "not supported" message.
DISPATCH STRATEGY. The recognised function IRIs are runtime values (RDFVocabulary.GEOSPARQL…ToString()), not compile-time constants, so they cannot be C# switch case labels without hardcoding (and thereby duplicating) the IRI strings. The dispatch is therefore driven by static lookup tables built ONCE from the vocabulary: a unary table, a binary table, and the two relation-family tables (Egenhofer, RCC8). Only the three argument-shaped functions (distance/buffer/relate), which each have bespoke argument handling, are matched individually.
Graph-pattern half of the SPARQL parser: the WHERE clause and the OPTIONAL/UNION/MINUS/GRAPH group-graph-pattern algebra.

Grouping half of the SPARQL parser: the GROUP BY clause (which materializes the single and absorbs the aggregates parked by the SELECT projection) and the HAVING clause (whose restricted comparison conditions are attached, as having-clauses, to the matching aggregators).
SPARQL grammar:
[19] GroupClause ::= 'GROUP' 'BY' GroupCondition+ [20] GroupCondition ::= BuiltInCall | FunctionCall | '(' Expression ('AS' Var)? ')' | Var [21] HavingClause ::= 'HAVING' HavingCondition+ [22] HavingCondition ::= Constraint // = BrackettedExpression | BuiltInCall | FunctionCall
Model-imposed limits (the flat model groups on bare variables and filters via per-aggregator having-clauses): a GroupCondition that is not a bare Var (an (expr AS ?v), a bare expression, a built-in or a function call) is NOT representable; a HAVING condition that is not a conjunction of (AGGREGATE OP value) comparisons (e.g. disjunctions, non-aggregate constraints, or an aggregate not present in the SELECT projection) is NOT representable. Each such case raises an explicit .
Solution-modifier half of the SPARQL parser: the trailing ORDER BY / LIMIT / OFFSET clauses of a SELECT query.
Prologue half of the SPARQL parser: the BASE/PREFIX declarations and the re-attachment of the declared prefixes onto the parsed query.

summary.para: Property-path half of the SPARQL parser: the verb of a triples block can be a full SPARQL 1.1 Path expression rather than a single predicate. This file parses the W3C SPARQL 1.1 path grammar directly into RDFSharp's recursive tree (the model represents every spec-legal path shape, so there is no lowering step and no rejected forms).

SPARQL 1.1 grammar (W3C §19.8 — the SINGLE source of truth here, NOT the printer):
[88] Path ::= PathAlternative [89] PathAlternative ::= PathSequence ( '|' PathSequence )* [90] PathSequence ::= PathEltOrInverse ( '/' PathEltOrInverse )* [91] PathElt ::= PathPrimary PathMod? [92] PathEltOrInverse ::= PathElt | '^' PathElt [93] PathMod ::= '?' | '*' | '+' [94] PathPrimary ::= iri | 'a' | '!' PathNegatedPropertySet | '(' Path ')' [95] PathNegatedPropertySet ::= PathOneInPropertySet | '(' ( PathOneInPropertySet ( '|' PathOneInPropertySet )* )? ')' [96] PathOneInPropertySet ::= iri | 'a' | '^' ( iri | 'a' )
The W3C grammar has NO {n,m} cardinality on paths — PathMod is exactly '?' | '*' | '+'.

member.summary: SELECT-form half of the SPARQL parser: the body of a SELECT query — the optional DISTINCT/REDUCED modifier, the projection (* wildcard or variable list), the WHERE clause, and the trailing solution modifiers — assembled into an RDFSelectQuery once the 'SELECT' keyword has been dispatched.

SERVICE half of the SPARQL parser: a ServiceGraphPattern delegates the evaluation of an inner group graph pattern to a remote SPARQL endpoint (federated query). It maps onto the first-class algebra node , modeling the grammar in full.
SPARQL grammar:
[59] ServiceGraphPattern ::= 'SERVICE' 'SILENT'? VarOrIri GroupGraphPattern [107] VarOrIri ::= Var | iri
All three forms are representable: a concrete IRI endpoint or a variable endpoint (SERVICE ?ep {…}, resolved at runtime from the surrounding bindings), an inner pattern of any shape (pattern group, sub-select, UNION/OPTIONAL/MINUS tree), and a nested SERVICE. SILENT maps to the endpoint's error behavior.

SubSelect half of the SPARQL parser: a nested SELECT query used as the sole content of a group graph pattern (GroupGraphPattern ::= '{' ( SubSelect | GroupGraphPatternSub ) '}'). A SubSelect becomes a subquery member (): the engine evaluates it independently and joins its projected bindings with the sibling members of the enclosing group.
Triples half of the SPARQL parser: the basic graph pattern (predicate-object/object lists) and the blank-node / collection desugaring.

summary.para: RDFQueryParser is responsible for turning a SPARQL 1.1 query string into the corresponding RDFQuery/RDFOperation object-model instance. It is the single entry point of the text-to-model pipeline: callers pass a raw SPARQL command string and receive a fully-built, engine-ready query.

The lexer reuses RDFTurtle's low-level term-parsing infrastructure (ParseURI, ParseValue, the pushback reader …) through a thin adapter (), so that IRI, literal and prefixed-name parsing are shared between the two parsers rather than duplicated.

member.name: F:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.AggregatorKeywords
member.summary: The seven SPARQL aggregate function names (case-insensitive). Membership of this set is what distinguishes an aggregate projection (COUNT(?x) AS ?c) from an ordinary computed projection (STRLEN(?x) AS ?c) at the SELECT-projection dispatch point.

member.name: T:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFParsedAggregator
member.summary: A function-agnostic snapshot of a parsed aggregate: which function (the uppercased keyword, e.g. "COUNT"/"GROUP_CONCAT"), over which single variable, whether DISTINCT, and (GROUP_CONCAT only) the separator. The projection variable is intentionally absent — it is supplied later by the caller via (projection path), or never (HAVING match path).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseAggregator(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses a single aggregate (the reader must be positioned on the function name): the function keyword, the mandatory parentheses, an optional DISTINCT, the SINGLE-variable argument, and — for GROUP_CONCAT only — an optional ; SEPARATOR = "..." clause. Returns the function-agnostic descriptor; the caller decides whether to materialize it (projection) or merely match it (HAVING).
member.exception: When the aggregate is malformed, or uses a form the flat model cannot represent (COUNT(*), expression argument).

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.BuildAggregator(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFParsedAggregator,RDFSharp.Query.RDFVariable)
member.summary: Materializes a parsed aggregate into the matching concrete , binding it to the given projection variable and propagating the DISTINCT flag. MIN/MAX default to the numeric flavor (SPARQL has no syntax to select the string flavor). GROUP_CONCAT carries its separator (default " ").

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.MatchesAggregator(RDFSharp.Query.RDFAggregator,RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFParsedAggregator)
member.summary: Returns true when the given (already built) aggregator is of the function kind described by the parsed descriptor AND aggregates over the same variable: the matching predicate used by HAVING to attach a having-clause to the aggregator that the SELECT projection already declared.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.TryPeekAggregatorKeyword(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Peeks at the upcoming token and returns the recognized aggregate keyword (uppercased) when it is one of the seven aggregate function names, restoring the reader to its prior position; returns the empty string otherwise. Used at the SELECT-projection '(' to choose between the aggregate path and the ordinary computed-projection (expression) path.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ReadAggregatorKeyword(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Reads a maximal run of ASCII letters AND underscores starting at the current position (the reader is left on the first character that is neither). Unlike — which stops at the underscore — this lets GROUP_CONCAT be read as a single token. Does NOT skip leading whitespace.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseAskQuery(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the body of an ASK query (the 'ASK' keyword has already been consumed by the dispatcher): the optional dataset clauses (rejected as non-representable), the WHERE clause, the trailing solution modifiers (GROUP BY / HAVING / ORDER BY / LIMIT / OFFSET) and the trailing query-level VALUES. The prologue's declared prefixes are re-attached so the query re-serializes its prologue identically.
member.exception: When a DatasetClause is present, the WHERE clause is malformed, or unexpected content trails the query.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RejectDatasetClause(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Rejects a leading DatasetClause (FROM / FROM NAMED) — the clause between the SELECT/ASK header and the WHERE clause. It is deliberately NOT supported: FROM/FROM NAMED instruct a SPARQL endpoint to procure (dereference/compose) its dataset on-the-fly, whereas RDFSharp is the evaluation engine over the data source you provide (graph/store/federation), not an endpoint. The equivalent scoping is expressed with GRAPH patterns over a store, so the clause is redundant here.
member.exception: When the next token is the FROM keyword.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RejectTrailingContent(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Requires end-of-input after an ASK query's WHERE clause, solution modifiers and trailing VALUES have all been consumed. Anything still left is genuinely unexpected; rejecting it (rather than relying on a fixed keyword list) avoids silently dropping it, since does not enforce end-of-input itself.
member.exception: When any significant content remains at the end of the ASK query.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseBind(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternGroup)
member.summary: Parses a BIND(expression AS ?var) assignment and attaches it to the target pattern group as an member: the engine evaluates the expression per-solution and binds its value to the variable, extending the group's solution mapping. SPARQL grammar: Bind ::= 'BIND' '(' Expression 'AS' Var ')'. The full expression grammar (boolean / comparison / arithmetic / built-ins / GeoSPARQL) is reused verbatim via , sharing the very same machinery as FILTER and the SELECT projection.
member.exception: When the parentheses, the mandatory 'AS' keyword, or the result variable are missing/malformed.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseValues(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFPatternGroup)
member.summary:
Parses a VALUES inline-data block and attaches it to the target pattern group as an member. SPARQL grammar:
InlineData ::= 'VALUES' DataBlock DataBlock ::= InlineDataOneVar | InlineDataFull InlineDataOneVar ::= Var '{' DataBlockValue* '}' InlineDataFull ::= ( NIL | '(' Var* ')' ) '{' ( '(' DataBlockValue* ')' | NIL )* '}' DataBlockValue ::= iri | RDFLiteral | NumericLiteral | BooleanLiteral | 'UNDEF'
(the 'VALUES' keyword has already been consumed by the dispatcher). The compact one-variable form and the extended multi-variable form share the same column-oriented model.
member.exception: When the block is malformed or a row's arity does not match the variable list.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseDataBlock(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses a standalone DataBlock (the part of VALUES after the keyword) and returns it as a freestanding , without attaching it anywhere. This is the shared entry point used both by an in-pattern-group VALUES (via ) and by the trailing query-level ValuesClause (SELECT ... WHERE { ... } VALUES ..., parsed in ParseSelectQuery).
member.exception: When the block is malformed or a row's arity does not match the variable list.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseInlineDataOneVar(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the compact one-variable inline-data form Var '{' DataBlockValue* '}' and returns the resulting single-column . Each value becomes one row of that single column; an UNDEF token becomes a null (unbound) binding. An empty value list (VALUES ?v { }) yields a declared-but-empty column (zero rows): a legal SPARQL block whose meaning is "zero solutions".

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseInlineDataFull(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the extended multi-variable inline-data form '(' Var* ')' '{' ( '(' DataBlockValue* ')' | NIL )* '}' and returns the resulting . Rows are read tuple-by-tuple and then transposed into the column-oriented model (one call per declared variable); each row's arity must equal the number of declared variables, and UNDEF tokens become null bindings. The variable list may be NIL (VALUES () { ... }): with zero variables the rows are empty-domain identity mappings, whose count is carried explicitly (no column to derive it from). An empty row list yields a "zero solutions" block.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseInlineDataRow(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,System.Int32)
member.summary: Parses a single parenthesised data row '(' DataBlockValue* ')' of an extended VALUES block and returns its values in declaration order (an UNDEF token yields a null entry). The row's arity must match , the number of variables the block declared.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseDataBlockValue(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseConstructQuery(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the body of a CONSTRUCT query (the 'CONSTRUCT' keyword has already been consumed by the dispatcher): the graph template, the optional dataset clauses (rejected as non-representable), the WHERE clause, and the trailing solution modifiers (only LIMIT/OFFSET are representable). The prologue's declared prefixes are re-attached so the query re-serializes its prologue identically.
member.exception: When the template, WHERE clause, dataset clause or a solution modifier is malformed/non-representable.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseConstructTemplate(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFConstructQuery)
member.summary:
Parses an explicit ConstructTemplate — the { ConstructTriples? } block of the LONG form — and attaches every triple it produces to as a TEMPLATE pattern.
The whole triple machinery (predicate-object/object lists, the a verb, blank nodes and collections) is reused verbatim via ; emission is diverted into the context's so ground triples survive (see the sink's documentation). Property paths and non-triple elements are not allowed by the template grammar and are rejected.
member.exception: When the braces are unbalanced, or the template contains a property path or a non-triple element.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseConstructShortForm(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFConstructQuery)
member.summary:
Parses the SHORT form body 'WHERE' '{' TriplesTemplate? '}': the same triples serve BOTH as the graph template and as the WHERE pattern. The 'WHERE' keyword is mandatory in this form.
The triples are read once (through the template sink, so ground triples are preserved for the template); each is then added as a template pattern and, via a pattern group, as the WHERE clause body. Ground triples are naturally dropped from the WHERE group by (which keeps only variable-bearing patterns) — the correct behaviour for a graph pattern.
member.exception: When 'WHERE' is missing, the braces are unbalanced, or the triples contain a property path or a non-triple element.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseTemplateTriples(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary:
Reads a ConstructTriples run (the caller owns the surrounding braces) into a flat list of template instances. The context's template sink is installed for the duration of the read and removed afterwards, regardless of outcome.
Two template-only restrictions are enforced after the read: a property path (:p/:q) is illegal because ConstructTriples uses TriplesSameSubject (no paths) — paths are detected as members of the scratch group they would have populated; and any element that is not a plain triple (a FILTER / OPTIONAL / nested group etc., which leaves on the reader) is rejected because the next significant token is then not the closing brace.
member.returns: The template patterns read from the block, in document order.
member.exception: When the block contains a property path or a non-triple element.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseDescribeQuery(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext)
member.summary: Parses the body of a DESCRIBE query (the 'DESCRIBE' keyword has already been consumed by the dispatcher): the describe-terms (a * wildcard or a non-empty list of variables/IRIs), the optional dataset clauses (rejected as non-representable), the OPTIONAL WHERE clause, and the trailing solution modifiers (only LIMIT/OFFSET are representable). The prologue's declared prefixes are re-attached so the query re-serializes its prologue identically.
member.exception: When the describe-terms, WHERE clause, dataset clause or a solution modifier is malformed/non-representable.

member.name: M:RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.ParseDescribeTerms(RDFSharp.Query.RDFQueryParser.RDFQueryParserContext,RDFSharp.Query.RDFDescribeQuery)
member.summary:
Parses the describe-terms of a DESCRIBE query — either the * wildcard (modeled by leaving empty) or a non-empty list of VarOrIri items (variables and/or IRIs) — and attaches each item to .
DISAMBIGUATION. The term list is followed by keywords (WHERE / FROM / LIMIT / …), and a prefixed-name IRI (foaf:Person) starts with letters just like a keyword does. The two are told apart WITHOUT a keyword set: a letter run is a prefixed name iff the very next character is a : — otherwise it is a terminating keyword and ends the list.
member.exception: When neither '*' nor any describe-term is present, or a term is a literal.

member.exception: When the term is a literal instead of an IRI.

Parses a single FILTER Constraint into the it denotes.
A ( opens a BrackettedExpression: the parenthesised content is parsed by the full expression ladder (so ||/&&/! nest there as boolean expressions).
Otherwise the constraint is a bare BuiltInCall or FunctionCall — including the EXISTS / NOT EXISTS built-ins — which is parsed and (when it is a value-expression) wrapped in an .

The operand is a full GroupGraphPattern ('{' ( SubSelect | GroupGraphPatternSub ) '}'): it is parsed by the shared group machinery and mapped onto the expression's two constructors — a (GroupGraphPatternSub) or a (SubSelect). A UNION/OPTIONAL/MINUS at the head of the group parses to a binary algebra tree, which is represented as the legal SubSelect alternative by wrapping it into a SELECT * subquery.
